news.Title: STM to Report Q3 Earnings: Can Healthy Revenues Drive Growth?
news.Content:
STMicroelectronics N.V. STM is set to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29, before the opening bell. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered an earnings surprise of 19.23%.

The company is expected to report year-over-year revenue growth, supported by demand for artificial intelligence (AI) and data-center solutions. However, slower recovery in certain business segments and weaker production volumes could have weighed on overall performance.

Factors at Play

STMicroelectronics is expected to have benefited from increasing investments in AI and data-center infrastructure during the third quarter of 2026. Growing demand for high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor solutions could have supported sales during the quarter.

During the quarter under review, improving customer demand and opportunities across key end markets are likely to have supported STMicroelectronics' business performance. Its diversified product portfolio might have helped the company address changing customer requirements.

STMicroelectronics' continued investment in research and development during the to-be-reported quarter is expected to support product innovation, improve operational efficiency and strengthen its long-term growth prospects.

However, pricing pressures and fluctuations in customer inventories could have affected STMicroelectronics' performance during the quarter. Higher manufacturing costs and lower capacity utilization might also have put pressure on profitability.

For the September quarter, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for total revenues is pegged at $3.71 billion, indicating an increase from $3.19 billion recorded a year ago. The consensus mark for earnings is pegged at 40 cents per share, implying growth from 29 cents reported in the prior-year quarter.

news.Title: Is Silicon Motion Stock a Strong Buy Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 earnings after the closing bell on Oct. 28. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for sales and earnings is pegged at $532.8 million and $3.3 per share, respectively. Earnings estimates for SIMO for 2026 and 2027 have remained unchanged over the past 60 days.

SIMO Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Earnings Surprise History

The leading NAND flash controller designer has a modest trailing four-quarter earnings surprise history, having exceeded expectations on three occasions. It delivered a four-quarter earnings surprise of 13.96%, on average. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered an earnings surprise of 14.08%.

Earnings Whispers

Our proven model does not conclusively predict an earnings beat for SIMO for the third quarter. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the chances of an earnings beat. That is not the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

Silicon Motion currently has an ESP of 0.00% and carries a Zacks Rank #3. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the quarter, Silicon Motion unveiled its MonTitan SSD Reference Design Kit, targeting AI infrastructure with high-performance, scalable storage solutions. The kit helps accelerate SSD development, enabling faster data processing, improved efficiency and optimized storage performance for demanding AI workloads, data centers and next-generation computing systems.

The company is expected to benefit from growing demand for enterprise storage solutions, AI infrastructure and automotive applications in the third quarter of 2026. Management expects revenues to increase 15-20% sequentially, supported primarily by its Ferri automotive storage products, enterprise boot drive solutions and MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers. The ongoing commercial ramp of MonTitan, coupled with healthy customer order patterns across storage solutions, is expected to support the company's near-term performance.

SIMO's embedded storage business is another potential growth driver. The company continues to gain market share in eMMC and UFS controllers as NAND suppliers focus more resources on higher-priority memory products. However, rising NAND and DRAM prices remain a potential headwind. Higher component costs are making smartphones and PCs less affordable, particularly in lower-priced segments

Story Continues

Price Performance

Over the past year, SIMO has surged 81.9% compared with the industry's growth of 97.6%. It has underperformed peers like Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Western Digital Corporation WDC over this period. While Marvell has gained 157.5%, WDC has jumped 171.3%.

Key Valuation Metric

From a valuation standpoint, Silicon Motion appears to be trading at a premium relative to the industry and above its mean. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 12.17 forward earnings, higher than 9.6 for the industry but lower than the stock's mean of 22.81.

Investment Considerations

SIMO's expanding exposure to enterprise storage, automotive applications and AI infrastructure strengthens its long-term growth opportunity. The company's controller technology, established relationships with NAND manufacturers, and growing presence in higher-value storage solutions could help it capture demand as computing workloads become more storage-intensive. The increasing contribution of MonTitan and enterprise boot drive products also offers an opportunity to reduce dependence on consumer-oriented markets over time.

Profitability is another factor worth monitoring. Management expects the third quarter to benefit from a more favorable product mix, particularly the rising contribution of MonTitan and PCIe Gen5 controllers.

However, SIMO is exposed to volatility in the consumer market. Weak smartphone and PC demand, elevated memory prices, intense competition and uncertainty surrounding component availability could limit growth in established product categories.

End Note

Expanding enterprise storage operations, market-share gains in embedded controllers and increasing demand for automotive and AI-related storage solutions are major tailwinds as SIMO is set to release third-quarter results. Nevertheless, higher memory costs, weakness in consumer markets and the pace of enterprise product adoption remain key variables. SIMO's diversification strategy boosts prospects for the long run, but in the near term, the company demonstrates a balanced outlook. Long-term investors should hold on to the stock, but new investors should wait for a better entry point.

news.Title: BofA Names Preferred Picks Among European Chipmakers Ahead of Earnings
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Ahead of earnings, BofA Securities prefers STMicroelectronics NV (EPA:STMPA), Infineon (ETR:IFXGn), Tower Semiconductor (TASE:TSEM) and Nordic Semiconductor (OL:NOD) over Melexis.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

For the first three, the broker expects modest beats and raises, with limited upside to gross margins and slight upside to revenues coming from data center/AI as well as Autos and Industrial. A common thread across the group is pricing.

BofA notes that better pricing for large OEMs, meaning flat to up 5% versus the traditional 1-5% price decline, is already expected, so any upside beyond that would come as a positive surprise.

STMicroelectronics is expected to deliver a modest beat and raise, with data center as the main storyline. BofA thinks the market may expect STM to lift its DC revenue guide to $3 billion for CY27, in line with BofA's own estimate, driven by Optical.

The harder question is margins. BofA believes investors need confidence that gross margins can move above 40% next year, which could come from mix, since BofA believes optical gross margins are above 50%, and/or from pricing for large OEMs.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Infineon also looks set for a modest beat and raise, and here the AI angle is about power. BofA thinks the market may expect IFX to guide combined FY27E AI and server CPU power revenues of €3.5-4 billion, while BofA's own estimate of €4.1 billion sits above the top of that range. Pricing is where the picture becomes more nuanced.

BofA expects the Autos business, which makes up 75% of the ATV division, to pass on 5-10% inflation from foundries.

The Power business, the other 25% of ATV, may find it harder. BofA believes IFX could struggle to raise prices for tier-1 customers by more than 5%, given oversupply in IGBTs and political sensitivities around the Dresden fab's subsidies.

Tower Semiconductor is grouped with STM and IFX in expecting a modest beat and raise, reflecting the limited gross margin upside and slight revenue upside described above. The note offers no further company-specific detail on TSEM, so nothing beyond that is stated here.

Nordic Semiconductor is the one name with an explicit rating in the note: BofA reiterates its Buy. The thesis rests on continued EBITDA improvement, driven by operational leverage and mix. The recent trend supports it, with EBITDA margin rising to 18.1% in the third quarter from 15.4% in the second.

Story Continues

The contrast with Melexis explains why these four are favored. BofA maintains an "underperform" rating on Melexis because of its greater reliance on global SAAR units, which have recently been affected by weaker demand in China and Europe, and because its auto growth has continued to lag peers.

news.Title: Susquehanna Makes Strong Calls on AMD, Intel, Qualcomm
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Susquehanna is reshuffling price targets across the semiconductor sector ahead of earnings, raising its outlook for AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ), Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM ) and Skyworks Solutions while cutting targets for Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ), Onsemi, Cirrus Logic and Wolfspeed.

The firm raised AMD's target to $620 from $550 , Qualcomm's to $185 from $160 , and Skyworks' to $90 from $65 .

Intel's target was cut to $105 from $115 , while Onsemi was reduced to $120 from $150. Cirrus Logic and Wolfspeed were also lowered.

Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland said AI remains the biggest source of upside, but the broader semiconductor cycle is also improving.

The firm's SemiSIGnals data showed lead times expanding by roughly two weeks for a second consecutive quarter , while pricing actions are becoming more aggressive.

Susquehanna also expects additional price increases in the fourth quarter and into 2027.

The problem is that not every end market is participating equally.

PC demand is tracking below expectations, which could leave second-half client results for both AMD and Intel below normal seasonal patterns.

In response, both companies are shifting wafer capacity away from PCs and toward servers, where demand tied to agentic AI remains much stronger.

Susquehanna also expects ARM-based hyperscale CPUs to keep gaining share as they increasingly serve as host processors for custom AI accelerators.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of Susquehanna's note is the widening split between AI-driven data center demand and weaker consumer electronics .

For AMD, that is relatively favorable because server demand gives the company another avenue to offset softness in PCs.

For Intel, the same shift helps, but weaker client demand still creates more pressure on the near-term setup.

Qualcomm benefits from the high end of the handset market holding up better, although Susquehanna remains cautious on smartphones overall because of memory constraints and deteriorating demand in China.

For investors, the key things to watch are server revenue, wafer reallocation, semiconductor pricing, hyperscaler capex and whether PC and handset weakness becomes more severe .

The chip cycle still appears to be improving.

But increasingly, the strongest part of that recovery is concentrated around AI infrastructure rather than broad-based consumer demand.
